sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The passage is a two-paragraph ethnographic remark: 'the language of signs has reached a high state of development.. Not that there is any stereotyped method of signs — there is no more an universal sign language than an universal Naga language, and the signs used depend on the genius and personality of the speaker' (p. 291), plus an anecdote of a deaf man's signed complaint. No linguistic description of the signing, no prosody.
